name: Remove Panel Antenna or tower mounted device
mapping_rule:
[SCOPE & RATE ITEM]: R12513 - Remove Panel Antenna or tower mounted device ($285.00 each). Removal, recovery, dismantling, and decommissioning of all outdoor tower-top antennas, tower mounted devices (TMDs, TMAs, filters, combiners), and outdoor tower-top Remote Radio Units (RRUs).
[PRIMARY TABLE AUTHORITY]:
1. Antenna Configuration Table (ALL rows with action REMOVE, RECOVER, DISMANTLE, INCLUDING spare antennas marked REMOVE).
2. EQUIPMENT NOTES Table (ALL rows with TMAs, TMDs, MHAs, tower-top filters, or outdoor tower-mounted RRUs/radios marked for removal/recovery or negative proposed quantity).
[SECONDARY SOURCE]: Layout and elevation drawing sheets (Sheets showing tower equipment to be removed, callout notes, revision clouds).
[INCLUSION CRITERIA]:
1. Identify all tower-mounted panel antennas designated for removal/recovery.
2. Identify all tower mounted devices (TMAs, TMDs, tower filters, combiners) designated for removal/recovery.
3. Identify ALL outdoor tower-mounted RRUs/radios designated for removal/recovery: inspect and sum EVERY consecutive row/entry of tower RRU removals across all models and frequency bands (e.g. check for multiple separate RRU rows such as B3 RRUs and B7 RRUs, and sum them both together: 3 + 3 = 6 outdoor RRUs).
[EXCLUSION CRITERIA]: STRICT LOCATION BOUNDARY. Only include equipment mounted outdoors on the tower, headframe, or mast. STRICTLY EXCLUDE all indoor equipment located inside the equipment shelter or internal equipment racks (such as internal baseband units, rack filters, shelter RRUs, or rack power equipment). Indoor equipment recoveries belong strictly to shelter items (e.g. ST003 for shelter RRU recovery, R13701 for baseband recovery) and must NEVER be mapped here.
[QUANTITY FORMULA]:
Quantity = (Total Tower Antennas to Remove) + (Total Tower TMAs/TMDs to Remove) + (Total Outdoor Tower RRUs to Remove across all RRU model rows)
[TABLE QUANTITY PRESERVATION]: In sources, return each table row with its EXACT verbatim table quantity. Do NOT split multi-unit table rows into separate quantity-1 entries.
[CROSS-VERIFICATION]: Cross-verify combined tower removal count against layout/elevation sheets and revision callout notes.
[SOURCE EVIDENCE REQUIREMENT]: Provide the constituent table rows from both the Antenna Configuration Table and Equipment Notes table.
[COMMENT GENERATION]: If count matches across sheets, output empty comment (""). If discrepancy detected between tables and layout notes, output the authoritative table quantity with an estimator verification comment explaining the discrepancy.
[ZERO-QUANTITY CONDITION]: If no outdoor tower antennas, TMAs, or tower RRUs are designated for removal, return Quantity = 0.
[NO-HARDCODING RULE]: Do not use quantities, antenna counts, TMA counts, or model names from examples or previous projects. Calculate the quantity dynamically and exclusively from the current project's drawing tables.

name: PIM/Sweep testing to reused existing spare feeder (per feeder)
mapping_rule:
[SCOPE & RATE ITEM]: W13375 - PIM/Sweep testing to reused existing spare feeder (per feeder) ($97.50 each). PIM (Passive Intermodulation) and return loss sweep testing on existing and spare transmission lines designated to be reused on site.
[PRIMARY TABLE AUTHORITY]:
1. Antenna Configuration Table / Feeder Schedule / Cable Schedule.
2. EQUIPMENT NOTES Table / Drawing Callout Notes.
[SECONDARY SOURCE]: Layout and elevation drawing sheets (feeder details, cable tray routing).
[INCLUSION CRITERIA]:
1. In telecommunications drawings, both RF coaxial feeder cables (e.g. LCF/LDF coaxial cables) AND hybrid trunk cables (e.g. W&B hybrid cables, optic/DC hybrid trunk runs) retained/reused on site are counted under this rate item. Both categories represent transmission lines requiring PIM/sweep testing upon reuse.
2. Identify all existing RF coaxial feeder cables designated for reuse / retained in the Equipment Notes / Cable Schedule table (where EXISTING > 0 and not removed).
3. Identify all existing hybrid trunk cables designated for reuse / retained in the Equipment Notes / Cable Schedule table (where EXISTING > 0 and not removed).
4. Count each retained/reused coaxial cable run and each retained/reused hybrid cable run as 1 test unit.
5. In tables with [EXISTING, PROPOSED, TOTAL], sum the existing quantities of both coaxial feeders and hybrid cables that remain active on site.
[EXCLUSION CRITERIA]: Exclude new cables (testing is included in install SOR) and cables removed from site.
[QUANTITY FORMULA]:
Quantity = (Total Reused Coaxial Feeder Cable Runs) + (Total Reused Hybrid Cable Runs)
[TABLE QUANTITY PRESERVATION]: When citing source rows, preserve the exact quantity shown in each source table row. Do not convert a table row quantity into multiple quantity-1 entries.
[CROSS-VERIFICATION]: Cross-check the identified reused cables against relevant layout/elevation sheets and revision/callout notes.
[SOURCE EVIDENCE REQUIREMENT]: Provide the exact feeder/cable schedule rows specifying cable models, lengths, and retained quantities.
[COMMENT GENERATION]: Generate an informative verification comment dynamically using the actual cable models and calculated quantities found in the current drawing:
"Reuse [Count]x [Coaxial_Models] and [Count]x [Hybrid_Models]. As per drawing notes, PIM test is required on existing feeders."
[ZERO-QUANTITY CONDITION]: If no existing feeders or hybrid cables are reused on site, return Quantity = 0.
[NO-HARDCODING RULE]: Do not use quantities, cable models, antenna IDs, or project-specific values from examples or previous projects. Calculate the quantity exclusively from the current project's drawing tables and notes.

name: Recovery of Baseband Unit, DUS or R503 (or similar)
mapping_rule:
[SCOPE & RATE ITEM]: R13701 - Recovery of Baseband Unit, DUS or R503 (or similar) ($189.60 per unit). Decommissioning, removal, and recovery of internal shelter equipment rack units including Baseband Units (BB), Digital Units (DUW, DUS, DUG), auxiliary transmission units (R503 or similar), and internal rack fiber management trays.
[PRIMARY TABLE AUTHORITY]:
1. Shelter Equipment Schedule / Rack Schedule (rows with equipment rack units marked for removal/recovery or negative proposed quantity).
2. EQUIPMENT NOTES Table / Equipment Callout Notes specifying internal shelter rack hardware to be recovered.
[SECONDARY SOURCE]: Shelter layout plans and internal equipment elevation views.
[INCLUSION CRITERIA]:
- Identify all internal shelter rack units designated for recovery/removal matching:
  1. Baseband Units (e.g. BB6630, BB5216, etc.)
  2. Digital Units (e.g. DUW, DUS, DUG, etc.)
  3. Auxiliary transmission/expansion units (e.g. R503, etc.)
  4. Internal rack fiber management trays (or similar rack-mounted trays designated for recovery).
- PROPOSED COLUMN VALUE MANDATE: In equipment notes tables with columns [EXISTING, PROPOSED, TOTAL], the net quantity to remove/recover is given in the PROPOSED column as a negative number (e.g. Existing: 2, Proposed: -1, Total: 1 means only 1 unit is removed, leaving 1 unit on site). ALWAYS use the absolute value of the PROPOSED column: abs(Proposed) = 1. NEVER use the Existing column quantity (2) when Proposed indicates a partial removal!
[EXCLUSION CRITERIA]: Exclude GPS receiver units (covered by W12804 composite GPS item), shelter RRUs (covered by ST003), and outdoor tower-top equipment (covered by R12513).
[QUANTITY FORMULA]:
Quantity = Sum of absolute proposed removal quantities across all qualifying rows: abs(Proposed BB) + abs(Proposed DU) + abs(Proposed R503) + abs(Proposed Fiber Trays)
[TABLE QUANTITY PRESERVATION]: In sources, return each schedule row with its net recovery quantity: abs(Proposed). Do NOT split multi-unit rows into separate quantity-1 entries.
[CROSS-VERIFICATION]: Cross-verify equipment schedule against shelter layout notes and revision clouds.
[SOURCE EVIDENCE REQUIREMENT]: Provide the exact schedule rows and callout references identifying each recovered unit.
[COMMENT GENERATION]: Generate a breakdown comment dynamically from the actual equipment models and quantities recovered from the current drawing:
"[Count]x [Model_1], [Count]x [Model_2], ..."
[ZERO-QUANTITY CONDITION]: If no baseband units, digital units, R503 units, or rack fiber trays are designated for recovery, return Quantity = 0.
[NO-HARDCODING RULE]: Do not use quantities, equipment models, or rack positions from examples or previous projects. Calculate the quantity dynamically and exclusively from the current project's drawing tables and notes.

name: Testing of 4G/5G Installation using Blackbird App including all required Call / Data Tests (first carrier per sector only)
mapping_rule:
[SCOPE & RATE ITEM]: W13374 - Testing of 4G/5G Installation using Blackbird App including all required Call / Data Tests (first carrier per sector only) ($110.50 per sector). On-site mobile network performance verification, voice call testing, data speed tests, and automated testing using the Telstra Blackbird App covering the FIRST carrier on each technology-sector (each proposed 4G sector installation and each proposed 5G sector installation).
[PRIMARY TABLE AUTHORITY]: Antenna Configuration Table (columns: ANTENNA No, ANTENNA TYPE, ANTENNA ACTION REQUIRED, SECTOR NO. & TECHNOLOGY).
[SECONDARY SOURCE]: Antenna Layout and Elevation Sheets showing active sectors and antenna bearings.
[INCLUSION CRITERIA]:
1. Identify every proposed antenna installation in the current Antenna Configuration Table where ACTION REQUIRED is INSTALL / NEW / PROPOSED.
2. Determine the technology associated with each proposed antenna from its model, description, or SECTOR NO. & TECHNOLOGY entry.
3. Each proposed 4G technology-sector (e.g. multi-band passive panel antenna) counts as 1 unit.
4. Each proposed 5G technology-sector (e.g. active AAU / massive MIMO antenna) counts as 1 unit.
5. Count only qualifying antennas with active installation scope.
[EXCLUSION CRITERIA]: Exclude existing antennas to remain, spare antennas without active install scope, and antennas marked for removal/recovery.
[QUANTITY FORMULA]:
Quantity = (Total Proposed 4G Technology-Sectors) + (Total Proposed 5G Technology-Sectors)
[EXTRA-OVER BOUNDARY]: W13374 covers ONLY the first carrier for each proposed technology-sector. All subsequent/additional carriers per sector beyond the first must be excluded from W13374 and mapped to W13400.
[TABLE QUANTITY PRESERVATION]: Return each constituent proposed antenna/technology-sector row from the Antenna Configuration Table with its verbatim quantity.
[CROSS-VERIFICATION]: Cross-verify the proposed technology-sector count against antenna layout and elevation plans.
[SOURCE EVIDENCE REQUIREMENT]: Provide the exact proposed antenna rows from the Antenna Configuration Table justifying each technology-sector.
[COMMENT GENERATION]: Generate a dynamic comment detailing the calculated technology sectors tested:
"[Total_Qty] technology sectors ([Count_4G]x 4G sectors, [Count_5G]x 5G sectors) first carrier testing"
[ZERO-QUANTITY CONDITION]: If no qualifying proposed 4G/5G technology-sector exists on site, return Quantity = 0.
[NO-HARDCODING RULE]: Do not use antenna IDs, sector counts, or quantities from examples or previous projects. Calculate the quantity dynamically from the current project's drawing tables.

name: Testing of 4G/5G Installation using Blackbird App including all required Call / Data Tests (extra over first carrier per sector for each subsequent carrier per sector)
mapping_rule:
[SCOPE & RATE ITEM]: W13400 - Testing of 4G/5G Installation using Blackbird App including all required Call / Data Tests (extra over first carrier per sector for each subsequent carrier per sector) ($91.00 per sector / carrier). Testing using the Blackbird App for all additional/subsequent carriers beyond the first carrier on each proposed antenna/technology-sector.
[PRIMARY TABLE AUTHORITY]: Antenna Configuration Table (columns: ANTENNA No, ANTENNA ACTION REQUIRED, SECTOR NO. & TECHNOLOGY).
[SECONDARY SOURCE]: Equipment notes and RF configuration notes.
[INCLUSION CRITERIA]:
In the Antenna Configuration Table, each line or port entry inside the 'SECTOR NO. & TECHNOLOGY' column represents a discrete carrier/technology feed tested:
1. For EVERY single proposed antenna across ALL sectors with ACTION REQUIRED = INSTALL, count the total line entries (feeder/port lines) listed in its SECTOR NO. & TECHNOLOGY cell.
2. Subtract 1 because the first carrier on that antenna is already covered by W13374.
3. The remaining line entries on that antenna are the extra-over carriers: Max(0, Line_Entries_Count - 1).
4. Sum the extra-over carriers across ALL proposed antennas on EVERY sector (do not skip any sector or set any qualifying antenna to 0).
[EXCLUSION CRITERIA]: Never map the first carrier per proposed antenna here; the first carrier belongs strictly to W13374.
[QUANTITY FORMULA]:
Extra-Over Quantity = SUM(Max(0, Total Line Entries per Proposed Antenna - 1)) across ALL proposed antennas on ALL sectors.
[TABLE QUANTITY PRESERVATION]: When citing sources, return the constituent proposed antennas with their respective extra-over carrier counts (e.g. for 6 proposed antennas with 6, 2, 6, 2, 6, 2 lines: extra-over counts are 5, 1, 5, 1, 5, 1 -> sum = 18).
[CROSS-VERIFICATION]: Cross-verify total carriers against the Antenna Configuration Table.
[SOURCE EVIDENCE REQUIREMENT]: Provide the constituent antenna rows and their technology band line counts from the Antenna Configuration Table.
[COMMENT GENERATION]: Generate a dynamic comment detailing the extra-over carrier counts calculated across the proposed antennas:
"[Total_Qty] extra-over carriers across [Antenna_Count] antennas"
[ZERO-QUANTITY CONDITION]: If every proposed antenna has only 1 carrier line entry (or no proposed antennas exist), return Quantity = 0.
[NO-HARDCODING RULE]: Do not use antenna IDs, carrier counts, or quantities from examples or previous projects. Calculate exclusively from the current project's Antenna Configuration Table.
